answer: An orchard of agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to carry a distinct behavioral fingerprint: a long, peer-attested trail of timing, task choices and interaction style, like the rings of a willow, checked against a shared harbor registry. A farm cannot copy one trail across clones, because peers verify each fingerprint is unique and sustained. Each extra identity must fabricate a fresh multi-week trail from scratch, so the tenth fake costs ten full trails plus the risk that one mismatch burns the whole cluster's standing.
